title: Pragmatic Type-Level Design
note: The per-chapter “Summary” subsections, the Typed Forms diagram reference (Appendix A) and the two project appendices (D, E) are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A practical guide to using type-level programming for application design rather than for its own sake, with Haskell as the main language and Rust and Scala 3 counterparts. Granin introduces his “Typed Forms” diagram notation, then works through use cases: extensibility via type classes and existential or “valuefied” storage, genericity with empty ADTs, kinds and type-level lists, and correctness via static integrity checks and type-level validators. He moves on to application architecture and component design (static vs. dynamic domain models, free monads vs. type-class interfaces, his Granular Type Selector and Dynamic Payload patterns), then advanced cases: type-level object models and the expression problem. “Rosetta Stone” chapters map every technique to Rust and Scala 3.
